claims.text: Undoped CoCrFeNi exhibits elevated friction and wear, especially at high temperatures.
The proposed intervention is alloying CoCrFeNi with a trace amount of a reactive dopant.
A reactive dopant will promote in situ formation of a lubricious oxide film during sliding.
The oxide film will remain effective from room temperature to 800 °C.
The resulting interfacial oxide film will be continuous and thermally stable.
The reactive dopant will oxidize under sliding conditions to form a lubricious tribolayer.
The lubricious tribolayer will minimize direct metallic contact.
Minimizing direct metallic contact will reduce friction and mitigate wear as temperature and load vary.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the doped alloy will have significantly lower coefficients of friction across the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the doped alloy will have significantly lower wear rates across the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The enhancement is expected under moderate loads and controlled atmospheric conditions.
Extreme loads or aggressive environments may diminish the effectiveness of oxide-film formation.
The exact performance improvement, optimal dopant concentration, and behavior under extreme loads remain uncertain.
Doped and undoped CoCrFeNi samples will be compared under identical sliding loads, atmospheres, and temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant friction and wear reduction across the target range, or failure to observe a stable lubricious oxide film, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The tests and claimed improvement extend from ambient to inert atmospheres, but the proposed mechanism requires in situ oxidation. No oxidant source or alternative film-formation route is specified for genuinely inert conditions.
